qs.q: Which biochemical marker is characteristically and most markedly elevated in the serum of a patient with active Paget's disease of bone?
qs.e: Alkaline phosphatase is markedly elevated in Paget's disease due to high bone turnover and increased osteoblastic activity. Serum calcium and phosphate levels typically remain within the normal reference range.

qs.q: In Paget's disease of bone, which marker is most characteristically elevated? ---
qs.e: Paget's disease of bone is characterized by high bone turnover, leading to a markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase.

qs.q: Paget's disease of bone characteristically shows
o: Very elevated ALP with normal levels
qs.e: Markedly elevated ALP reflects intense bone turnover; serum calcium is usually normal at rest.

qs.q: Paget's disease of bone is characterized by
o: Defective osteoblasts producing weak unmineralized matrix
Autoimmune destruction of osteocytes within bone
Decreased bone turnover with dense uniform sclerosis
Disordered bone remodeling with excessive osteoclasts
qs.e: Paget's: paramyxovirus implicated. Phases: osteolytic (osteoclast excess) → mixed → osteosclerotic. Characteristic histology: mosaic/jigsaw pattern of lamellar bone. Markedly elevated ALP (bone formation marker). Features: bone pain, skull enlargement (hat size increase), bowing of tibia (saber shin), deafness (CN VIII compression), high-output cardiac failure (increased vascularity). Complications: osteosarcoma (<1%
